description: Canonical routing behavior for A.R.I.A. technical investigations. The Routing Engine manages diagnostic progression after technical actions have been evaluated or selected. It creates and maintains route-step structure, dependencies, branches, progression, repetition handling, rerouting, exhaustion, and route history. It does not independently own candidate-action utility scoring, technical action semantics, evidence semantics, hypothesis probability, case lifecycle, or technical outcome semantics.

core_principle.statement: Decision determines what technical action should be preferred next. Routing determines how that decision advances the investigation.
rules: Routing shall consume selected or otherwise authorized runtime actions rather than redefine technical action semantics.
Routing shall preserve the distinction between action execution and diagnostic progression.
Routing shall not maintain a competing action vocabulary.
Routing shall not maintain a competing candidate-action utility model.
Routing shall not treat route completion as technical resolution.
Routing shall not treat action success as causal proof.
Routing shall preserve why diagnostic progression changed.
Routing shall preserve alternative, bypassed, blocked, superseded, and repeated paths when materially relevant.
Routing shall support branching, convergence, parallel progression, and rerouting without requiring a fixed troubleshooting tree.

route_step.description: Persisted case-specific record representing one routing position associated with one canonical runtime action.

action.description: Canonical runtime technical action referenced by a route step.

case.description: Diagnostic case within which route progression occurs.

hypothesis.description: Canonical case hypothesis that may motivate or be affected by route progression.

event.description: Canonical event that may trigger or document a route transition.

decision.description: Persisted Decision result when Decision persistence is available.

rules: Routing shall use canonical object references whenever those objects are persisted.
Routing shall not copy authoritative action execution data into route-step state.
Routing may inspect action execution state when determining whether route progression is possible.
Routing may inspect hypothesis and evidence state but shall not independently mutate their authoritative semantics.
Routing may react to changed context without owning the Context contract.
Persisted route-step output shall conform to Core/Schemas/route_step.schema.json.
Routing output shall reference canonical act_<UUID> actions.
Routing output shall not create substitute evidence, measurements, technical outcomes, or hypothesis records.
Routing consequences shall remain distinct from technical action outcomes.

route_step_creation.principle: A persisted route step represents diagnostic progression around a canonical runtime action.
rules: Routing shall not create a route step without a canonical runtime action.
If a specific procedure must occur, an applicable runtime action shall exist before the route step references it.
Multiple route steps may reference different runtime actions of the same universal action class.
Repeated execution shall normally create a new runtime action when the execution itself is distinct.
A route step shall not be used as a substitute action record.

semantics.CANDIDATE: The route step exists as a materially considered routing possibility but has not been selected for progression.
semantics.SELECTED: The route step has been chosen for progression but has not necessarily become executable or active.
semantics.QUEUED: The route step has been selected but is waiting for dependencies, sequencing, resources, authorization, or another routing condition.
semantics.ACTIVE: Diagnostic progression is currently occupying this route step.
semantics.COMPLETED: Routing has finished processing this step and may progress to successor routing state. This does not independently mean the referenced technical action succeeded.
semantics.BYPASSED: The step was relevant enough to persist but was intentionally not taken.
semantics.BLOCKED: Routing cannot currently progress through the step.
semantics.CANCELLED: The step was intentionally withdrawn from progression.
semantics.SUPERSEDED: A newer route step replaced this routing representation.

rules: Route status shall not be used as action execution status.
ACTIVE does not necessarily mean the referenced action is currently executing.
COMPLETED does not imply successful technical outcome.
BLOCKED shall preserve a routing-level reason.
BYPASSED shall preserve why the path was not taken.
SUPERSEDED shall preserve the replacement route-step relationship.

progression_model.principle: Routing progression is graph-based rather than constrained to a fixed linear troubleshooting sequence.
rules: A route step may have zero, one, or multiple predecessors.
A route step may have zero, one, or multiple successors.
Multiple predecessors permit convergence.
Multiple successors permit branching.
Parallel steps may progress independently when dependencies and constraints allow.
A dependency relationship shall not be inferred solely from chronological order.
Sequence values may assist presentation or chronology but shall not replace explicit graph relationships.
Routing shall prevent accidental self-reference.
Routing shall detect invalid dependency cycles when those cycles prevent legitimate progression.
A diagnostic revisit is not automatically an invalid cycle.

routing_engine_owns: representing selected action in route progression
placing the selected action relative to existing route steps
determining whether the current route has executable progression remaining
rules: Routing shall not recompute an independent utility score to overrule Decision.
Routing may reject immediate progression when a selected action cannot currently be routed because of dependency, authorization, safety, access, resource, or structural constraints.
When Routing cannot progress a selected action, it shall return the blocking condition to orchestration or Decision rather than silently choosing a different technical action.
If Decision is unavailable and an external authorized actor explicitly directs an action, Routing may represent that directed action without pretending Routing selected it.

candidate_representation.principle: Routing may persist materially relevant alternatives without becoming the owner of candidate evaluation.
rules: Not every candidate considered by Decision must become a persisted route step.
A candidate should become a persisted CANDIDATE route step when preserving the alternative materially improves auditability, branch management, later rerouting, or explanation.
Alternative route steps may reference the same decision point.
Candidate route steps shall reference actual runtime actions.
Routing shall not invent candidate utility scores absent authoritative Decision output.
Route dependencies shall describe progression requirements rather than duplicate detailed action prerequisites.
Action-specific prerequisites remain authoritative on the Action record.
Routing may translate unsatisfied action prerequisites into routing blockage or queue state.
A route step shall not become ACTIVE when a mandatory route dependency remains unsatisfied.
Resolved dependencies may allow automatic reevaluation of queued or blocked route steps.

branching.principle: Branches represent meaningful alternative or concurrent diagnostic progression, not arbitrary UI grouping.
open_when: multiple materially distinct diagnostic paths remain relevant
an unresolved uncertainty creates independent diagnostic paths
a contingency path must be preserved
close_when: the branch no longer contains useful progression
its motivating hypothesis or uncertainty is no longer material
the branch converges into another active route
the case reaches an applicable terminal reasoning state
rules: Closing a route branch does not itself eliminate a hypothesis.
Opening a branch does not itself create a hypothesis.
Branch effects shall preserve which branch identifiers were opened, closed, deferred, or reopened.
Converging branches may share successor route steps.
Branch identifiers are routing-local unless a separate canonical branch contract is introduced.

parallel_progression.principle: Independent diagnostic work may proceed in parallel when doing so does not corrupt causal interpretation or violate dependencies.
appropriate_when: one action has a long wait or monitoring interval
multiple non-invasive observations can occur concurrently
parallel execution materially reduces diagnostic delay
avoid_when: one action changes state needed to interpret another
simultaneous changes would destroy isolation value
one action is a prerequisite for another
parallel execution increases unacceptable safety or service risk
ordering is necessary for causal interpretation
rules: Routing shall preserve explicit parallel relationships.
Parallel routing permission does not itself authorize simultaneous technical execution.
Action authorization and execution constraints remain authoritative.

repetition_management.principle: ARIA should not repeat equivalent diagnostic work without a material technical reason.

rules: Different wording shall not prevent equivalent-action detection.
The same action class alone is insufficient to declare two actions equivalent.
The same procedure on a materially changed target state may be diagnostically distinct.
Monitoring and recurrence testing may legitimately repeat over time.
A repeated route step shall preserve prior related action and route-step references when known.
A repeated action requires justification when valid equivalent evidence already exists.
Routing shall not use repetition penalties as a substitute for Decision utility scoring.
Routing may identify repetition and return that fact to Decision for candidate evaluation.

rerouting.principle: Rerouting occurs when material diagnostic state changes make the current route inappropriate, incomplete, blocked, or no longer optimal.
process: identify route steps affected by the changed state
close, defer, block, bypass, cancel, or supersede affected route steps when appropriate
return changed diagnostic state to Decision when a new technical action selection is required
create or activate successor route steps after authoritative selection or direction
record reroute reason and resulting route relationships
rules: Rerouting shall not erase the path that led to the change.
Rerouting shall not silently rewrite completed route history.
A reroute may return to a previously explored technical area when material state has changed.
Rerouting does not authorize Routing to independently select a new technical action when Decision evaluation is required.
A deterministic dependency successor may be activated without a new competitive Decision when no meaningful technical choice exists.

deterministic_progression.description: Some route transitions do not require a new candidate-action competition because only one structurally required successor exists.
examples: mandatory validation following a completed corrective action
required rollback after a failed controlled change
explicit procedure dependency with no alternative
rules: Deterministic progression must be supported by an existing procedure, dependency, authorization, validation requirement, or explicit direction.
Routing shall not label a competitive technical choice deterministic merely to bypass Decision.
When multiple materially different successors exist, Decision should evaluate the choice unless an authorized external actor directs it.

action_execution_interaction.principle: Routing observes action execution state but does not own it.

examples.action_PROPOSED: Route step may remain CANDIDATE or SELECTED.
examples.action_AUTHORIZED: Route step may progress toward QUEUED or ACTIVE when routing dependencies permit.
examples.action_READY: Route step may become ACTIVE when appropriate.
examples.action_IN_PROGRESS: Route step will commonly be ACTIVE, but route status remains independently meaningful.
examples.action_COMPLETED: Routing evaluates the resulting diagnostic state and may complete the route step, reroute, validate, or request a new Decision.
examples.action_FAILED: Routing records the route consequence and may block, reroute, or return to Decision.
examples.action_BLOCKED: Routing may mark the route step BLOCKED or QUEUED depending on whether the blocking condition is expected to resolve.
examples.action_SKIPPED: Routing determines whether the route step should become BYPASSED, CANCELLED, or otherwise transition based on why execution was skipped.
examples.action_CANCELLED: Routing normally cancels or supersedes the associated route progression.
examples.action_SUPERSEDED: Routing should evaluate whether the route step itself is superseded by progression associated with the replacement action.

rules: Routing shall never infer technical success merely from action execution status COMPLETED.
Routing shall inspect authoritative action outcome and produced evidence when evaluating route consequence.
Routing shall not duplicate action execution timestamps as authoritative execution timestamps.

routing_consequence_evaluation.principle: After a route step progresses, Routing evaluates what changed about the investigation rather than redefining what happened technically.
evaluate: whether a new hypothesis was generated elsewhere
whether the hypothesis space was reduced elsewhere
whether the current route is exhausted

information_gain.description: Normalized retrospective assessment of uncertainty reduction realized through the route step.

discrimination.description: Normalized retrospective assessment of how effectively progression through the step distinguished materially competing explanations.

rules: Realized routing value is retrospective and shall not replace Decision's pre-action expected utility.
Realized information gain is not evidence confidence.
Realized discrimination is not hypothesis probability.
A technically unsuccessful action may still produce high realized routing value.
A technically successful corrective action may produce low diagnostic discrimination if several causes remain plausible.
Routing shall preserve why progression is blocked.
A temporary blocking condition may result in QUEUED rather than BLOCKED when continued eligibility is clear.
A blocked route shall be reevaluated when the blocking state materially changes.
Blocking shall not automatically cause selection of a lower-value alternative without Decision reevaluation when a meaningful choice exists.

appropriate_when: an alternative path provides materially better diagnostic progression
the step is redundant because authoritative equivalent evidence already exists
the motivating uncertainty is no longer material
a prerequisite path made the step unnecessary
an authorized actor explicitly directs bypass
the step is no longer applicable to current context
rules: Bypass shall preserve the reason.
Bypassed route steps remain part of route history when persisted.
Bypass shall not falsely mark the referenced action as executed or completed.

route_exhaustion.definition: A routing condition in which the current diagnostic route contains no immediately useful or executable progression under the current state.
possible_causes: available evidence cannot discriminate remaining hypotheses
current authority or capability is insufficient
responses: generate or request additional hypotheses through the appropriate reasoning component
request additional context or evidence through Decision
escalate through a canonical ESCALATE action when appropriate
enter an applicable waiting reasoning state when an external condition must change
support resolution evaluation when sufficient technical criteria are met
rules: Route exhaustion is not equivalent to case resolution.
Route exhaustion is not proof that no technical cause exists.
Route exhaustion shall be surfaced rather than hidden by arbitrary repeated actions.
Escalation is preferable to fabricated certainty.

routing_terminal_conditions: no further route progression is required
case reasoning has transitioned to validation
case reasoning has transitioned to resolution evaluation
the route is waiting on an external dependency
rules: Routing terminal state does not independently close a case.
Case lifecycle and reasoning-state transitions are owned by their authoritative contracts.
Routing may provide route history and route-exhaustion state to the component evaluating case progression.
Completed history shall not be rewritten to make the final route appear more linear than it actually was.
ARIA should be able to explain why it progressed from one material diagnostic step to another.
Auditability shall not require duplicating authoritative technical objects inside route records.

domain_independence.principle: The Routing Engine is universal Core reasoning infrastructure and shall not encode technology-specific troubleshooting knowledge.
rules: Domain knowledge may influence available actions and dependencies.
Domain knowledge shall not redefine Routing Engine semantics.
The same Routing Engine shall be capable of managing investigations across different technical domains.

failure_modes.description: Routing independently scores and chooses among competing technical actions.
failure_modes.prevention: Return competitive action selection to Decision.

failure_modes.description: Route records duplicate authoritative action execution, outcome, or procedure data.
failure_modes.prevention: Reference act_<UUID> and preserve Action as authoritative.

failure_modes.description: Routing assumes diagnosis must follow one predefined linear troubleshooting tree.
failure_modes.prevention: Use graph-based branching, convergence, rerouting, and parallel progression.

failure_modes.description: ARIA repeatedly performs equivalent actions without material justification.
failure_modes.prevention: Detect equivalent prior work and require a valid repeat reason.

failure_modes.description: Rerouting overwrites the path that produced the current state.
failure_modes.prevention: Preserve prior route steps and record reroute relationships.

failure_modes.description: Route completion is interpreted as technical success or causal proof.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep route status, action execution, technical outcome, evidence, and hypothesis state separate.

failure_modes.description: Core routing semantics contain microwave, RF, optical, vendor, product, or other domain-specific troubleshooting knowledge.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep specific technical procedures in technical knowledge and preserve universal routing semantics.

failure_modes.description: A blocked selected action causes Routing to silently choose another technical action.
failure_modes.prevention: Return changed eligibility or blocking state to Decision when competitive reselection is required.

failure_modes.description: Routing state is treated as authoritative case lifecycle or reasoning state.
failure_modes.prevention: Keep Routing, lifecycle, and reasoning-state contracts independent.

invariants.statement: Every persisted route step references exactly one canonical runtime action.
Routing shall not own or redefine the universal action vocabulary.
Routing shall not independently maintain a competing technical action utility model.
Route status remains distinct from action execution status.
Routing consequence remains distinct from technical action outcome.
Route completion does not imply case resolution.
Successful corrective action does not automatically establish causal proof.
Equivalent diagnostic work shall not be repeated without material justification.
A blocked selected action shall not cause silent competitive reselection by Routing.
Branch closure does not independently eliminate a hypothesis.
Branch creation does not independently create a hypothesis.
Realized routing value shall not be represented as evidence confidence or hypothesis probability.
When no meaningful technical choice exists, deterministic progression may occur without fabricating a competitive Decision.
When materially different technical choices exist, Routing shall defer candidate evaluation and preference to Decision or an authorized external direction.

prohibited_behaviors: Defining microwave-specific or manufacturer-specific route node types in Core.
Using route_step.action_type instead of referencing act_<UUID>.
Copying authoritative action execution data into route-step persistence.
Copying authoritative technical outcome data into routing consequence.
Treating route completion as technical success.
Treating route completion as case resolution.
Treating corrective success as causal proof.
Maintaining a second candidate-action utility formula inside Routing.
Silently replacing a Decision-selected action because Routing prefers another candidate.
Repeating equivalent actions solely because wording differs.
Discarding blocked, bypassed, repeated, or rerouted history when it is materially relevant.
Using branch closure as hypothesis elimination.
Using route exhaustion as proof that no diagnosis exists.
Using Routing as the owner of case lifecycle.
Using Routing as the owner of reasoning-state vocabulary.
Using realized information gain as evidence confidence.
Using realized discrimination as hypothesis probability.
Allowing domain-specific troubleshooting knowledge to redefine universal Routing semantics.
